name: ScrollReveal.jsx
summary: Reusable Framer Motion wrapper that fades and slides its children up the first time they enter the viewport; used throughout the page sections.

name: SectionHeading.jsx
summary: Shared section header rendering a numbered eyebrow label over a large title whose last word is set in accent italic, revealed on scroll.

name: WorkflowSteps.jsx
summary: Small interactive explainer used in project case studies: clicking a step highlights it, advances a progress track, and announces its description to screen readers.

name: content.js
summary: Thin accessor over src/data/site.json that re-exports language-independent content (profile, sections, stack, experience tags, project metadata, last-updated date) and the featured project count.

name: About.jsx
summary: About section presenting translated intro paragraphs, a responsive profile photo with location caption, and animated stat cards in a bento layout.

name: Experience.jsx
summary: Experience section rendering translated career entries as a timeline, pairing each item by index with its language-independent tags from shared content.

name: Exploring.jsx
summary: Section describing what the author is currently exploring, showing a translated paragraph and a tag list inside a reveal-animated card.

name: Faq.jsx
summary: FAQ section listing translated question and answer cards written to be self-contained for people and AI assistants; the same items feed the FAQPage schema during pre-rendering.

name: Projects.jsx
summary: Projects section that splits translated project entries into detailed featured case-study cards and a compact grid of other projects, merging each with language-independent metadata such as tags, images, links, and an optional workflow explainer.

name: Controls.jsx
summary: Shared language switcher and theme toggle used by both the desktop nav bar and the mobile menu.

name: LanguageContext.jsx
summary: React context managing the active language, derived from the URL, with crossfaded switches, history integration, persistence, and document head updates.

name: ThemeContext.jsx
summary: Theme state layer that treats the document's data-theme attribute as an external store, staying consistent with the pre-paint inline script and dark-by-default pre-rendered HTML.

name: entry-server.jsx
summary: Server-side rendering entry used at build time by the pre-render script to produce the static HTML for each language.

name: translations.js
summary: Central i18n module that aggregates the per-language JSON copy and exposes the translations map, supported languages, default language, and language URL helper.

name: main.jsx
summary: Browser entry point that wraps App in theme, language, and motion providers, then hydrates pre-rendered markup or falls back to a fresh client render in development.

name: Navbar.jsx
summary: Floating glass navigation bar with section links and active-state highlighting that collapses into a mobile menu sheet below 960px.

name: CopyEmail.jsx
summary: Defines the contact email row: a mailto link plus a one-click copy button that confirms in place and falls back to the mail app when clipboard access is blocked.

name: Magnetic.jsx
summary: Provides a wrapper component that adds a magnetic hover effect to call-to-action buttons, limited to precise pointers and disabled under reduced motion.

name: RevealText.jsx
summary: Provides a CSS-only per-letter text reveal so the hero name animates from pre-rendered HTML without waiting for JavaScript.

name: SceneBoundary.jsx
summary: Provides the error boundary around the lazy three.js hero scene, so a failed chunk load leaves the CSS orb fallback visible rather than breaking the page.

name: Contact.jsx
summary: Implements the portfolio's closing contact section, combining localized copy with profile data for email, WhatsApp, phone, LinkedIn, and GitHub links.

name: Hero.jsx
summary: Implements the landing hero with an animated name, localized intro, and calls to action, deferring the three.js brain into a lazy chunk so 3D never competes with page content.

name: App.jsx
summary: Root React component module that assembles the single-page portfolio from its navbar, sections, technology marquee, and footer, shared by both the client and server render entries.

name: Marquee.jsx
summary: Reusable presentational component module providing the endlessly scrolling strip of technologies shown beneath the hero.

name: useActiveSection.js
summary: Custom React hook module that tracks which page section is currently in view so the navbar can highlight its matching link.

name: useGlowPointer.js
summary: Custom React hook module that drives the cursor-following glow on card borders by publishing pointer coordinates as CSS custom properties.

name: HeroScene.jsx
summary: React component that renders the hero's animated Three.js brain, loading its geometry through a Web Worker and running the WebGL scene with cortical shader waves, neuron pulses and pointer-driven rotation. It pauses off-screen, honours reduced motion, and leaves a CSS orb as the fallback when WebGL is unavailable.

name: brain.worker.js
summary: Web Worker that runs createBrain off the main thread on request and posts back the surfaces, neuron positions, edges and adjacency as plain serializable data.

name: brainGeometry.js
summary: Procedurally generates the hero brain's anatomy (folded hemispheres, cerebellum, brain stem) and a neuron network on the fold crests using seeded Perlin noise, so no model file has to be downloaded. Imported by both the worker and the main-thread scene.

name: GEO-ANALYSIS.md
summary: SEO and GEO audit of the deployed portfolio, combining measured Lighthouse scores with an estimated GEO readiness score of about 79/100. It also lists what is already in place and the remaining actions, most of which are off-site.

name: PORTFOLIO-REVIEW.md
summary: Design review of an earlier live build with scored areas, reference portfolios and a tiered action plan, plus code for the three most impactful changes. Its file references predate the later redesign and may not match the current source.

name: README.md
summary: Unmodified Vite React template README covering the official React plugins, the React Compiler and ESLint expansion. It says nothing about the portfolio itself; architect.md is the real project documentation.

name: architect.md
summary: Main architecture reference covering the tech stack, directory map, page layout, theme and language state, JSON content model, styling tokens, SEO build output and known gaps. It explains how to edit content and the index-matching rules that language files must follow.

name: index.html
summary: HTML template for the single-page app, holding fonts, icons, the manifest link and the module script that loads src/main.jsx. An inline script applies a saved light theme and redirects visitors landing on / to their language page, and placeholder comments mark where pre-rendered head and body are injected.

name: package.json
summary: npm manifest for the private ES module project, declaring React 19, Three.js, Framer Motion and lucide-react with Vite and ESLint tooling. Its build script chains the client build, the SSR build of src/entry-server.jsx and the prerender script.

name: vercel.json
summary: Vercel deployment configuration that sets the build command, the dist output directory and trailing slashes. It also applies security headers to all routes and long-lived cache headers to hashed assets and images.

name: en.json
summary: English content dictionary holding all UI strings, biography, experience, project case studies, FAQ and page metadata for the portfolio. It is the default-language reference whose keys and array lengths the French and Spanish files mirror.

name: es.json
summary: Spanish translation of the portfolio's content dictionary, covering navigation, biography, experience, project case studies, FAQ and es_ES page metadata with the same shape as the other language files.

name: fr.json
summary: French translation of the portfolio's content dictionary, covering navigation, biography, experience, project case studies, FAQ and fr_FR page metadata with the same shape as the other language files.

name: site.json
summary: Language-independent site data: profile contact details and photos, section order, tech stack, experience tags, project metadata, canonical URL, default language and the structured person details. Its experience and project arrays are matched by position to the translated items in the language files.

name: eslint.config.js
summary: ESLint flat config that lints JS and JSX with the recommended, React Hooks and React Refresh rule sets, ignoring dist, .ssr and claude-seo. It also relaxes no-unused-vars for the `m` motion alias, which core ESLint cannot see used as a JSX tag.

name: 404.html
summary: Static, self-styled not-found page marked noindex, with links back to the English, French and Spanish versions of the portfolio.

name: robots.txt
summary: Crawler policy allowing all user agents and explicitly allowing AI search and assistant bots such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot. It also points crawlers to the site's sitemap.xml.

name: site.webmanifest
summary: Web app manifest declaring the portfolio's name, standalone display mode, navy theme colors and 192px and 512px icons.

name: prerender.mjs
summary: Post-build script that renders the SSR bundle into one static HTML page per language with SEO head tags and JSON-LD. It also generates sitemap.xml, llms.txt and llms-full.txt from src/data, then removes the temporary .ssr output.

name: App.css
summary: Minimal stylesheet imported by the App component that only resets the body margin and sets its display to block.

name: index.css
summary: Global stylesheet for the whole site, defining the Deep Ocean design tokens with dark and light themes. It styles every section from nav and hero through projects, FAQ and footer, along with responsive breakpoints, animations and reduced-motion handling.

name: vite.config.js
summary: Vite build configuration that enables the React plugin and maps the `@` import alias to the src directory.
